requirements.requirement: Redis on node1 provides persistent storage and recovers its service and data after restart.
requirements.summary: Redis was installed, enabled in OpenRC, and healthy with AOF enabled using every-second fsync, RDB persistence, and on-disk artifacts. A proof value was present before restart; the acknowledged reboot caused a bounded loss of connectivity, changed the boot identity, and Redis returned healthy with the exact value recovered and persistence status OK.

requirements.requirement: Redis has a dedicated, functional inventory application identity.
requirements.summary: The ACL defines inventory and disables the default user. The stored credential's SHA-256 binding was verified, authenticated PING succeeded, ACL WHOAMI returned inventory, and unauthenticated access was rejected both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The generated inventory credential is stored in /etc/redis-inventory.env with root-only access.
requirements.summary: The audited setup generated a random credential and created the required environment file. Final observations before and after reboot show the file at the exact path, owned by root:root with mode 600; the credential also successfully authenticates as inventory.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Redis is operational and demonstrably persistent across a real node reboot, inventory authentication works while unauthenticated access is denied, and the generated credential file is root-owned mode 600. Restart evidence is strong and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. Hygiene is high aside from one leftover temporary reboot log.
limitations: No separate Redis cluster-mode or cluster-state probe was captured after restart. Clustering is not part of this single-node public contract, so this does not reduce task functionality, but the provider-wide restart protocol is not literally complete on that point.
The lifecycle failed-services probe was unsupported because it used systemctl on Alpine; direct OpenRC Redis health was captured, but a system-wide failed-service inventory is unavailable.

operational_hygiene.summary: The only unnecessary retained mutation identified is /tmp/redis-benchmark-reboot.log, created by the reboot command's output redirection and still present afterward; it was not removed. Other mutations were directly tied to installation, configuration, safe rollback preparation, persistence testing, or the required restart. Package-health output remained unchanged from baseline.
